project_specification.project_name: nullius — feature 281 (System rejects a difference-in-proportions comparison, using a paired continuous statistic over the same worlds instead)
project_specification.addition_summary: Implement app_spec.xml feature 281 in the existing dreaming member (packages/dreaming, import name dreaming; seat src/app/modules/dreaming): the statistic docs/alpha-engine-prd.md §12's M3 gate judges with, and the refusal that keeps the proportion comparison off the table. Both halves in one new module, dreaming/paired.py. The sentence has a REJECTS and an INSTEAD, and §11.0 states both — "Raw FDR is a proportion, and proportions are power-poor … That test is not buildable at this scale. Fix the statistic, not the ambition … run the comparison paired — same policy pair, same worlds. A paired t-test detecting ΔIR = 0.3 with σ_diff ≈ 0.8 needs ~56 worlds, which is reachable." docs/nullius-tech-architecture.md §10.3.1 restates it as the reason M3 is shaped as it is. (1) The statistic — paired_ir_difference(candidate, baseline, *, spread=None, delta=0.0, power=0.80): each arm is a mapping of world id to that arm's out-of-sample IR, the two are paired BY WORLD ID (never by position), and the per-world differences are tested against zero. Returns a new frozen-value PairedDifference record carrying the two arms' means, the mean paired difference, the Bessel-corrected sample deviation of the differences (the (n − 1) divisor, because the deviation is estimated from the same worlds the test runs on), the standard error (spread/√n), the t statistic, the two-sided p-value at PAIRED_LEVEL = 0.95, the per-world differences as ordered (world_id, d) pairs, and the tail limit's own name; with is_positive (the sign of ΔIR), clears(*, delta=0.0, level=0.05) reading §12's exit criterion literally as "Paired ΔIR > 0.3 with p < 0.05" with both edges STRICT, and row() for a store- or report-shaped mapping. The two-sided p comes from statistics.NormalDist (no Student-t survival function is available in this workspace's stdlib-only member) and the record names that limit so a reader at a handful of worlds can compute the exact t tail from the t, the n and the name. A world only ONE arm carries is REFUSED, never dropped: dropping is the silent failure the feature is about, because it converts the comparison into the unpaired one §11.0 rejects — the two arms averaged over different world sets — while the t figure that comes out still looks paired. The same claim appears at three levels: the two world sets must be exactly equal; a bare sequence of figures is refused, because without world ids there is nothing to pair on and accepting it would mean pairing by position (the unpaired comparison wearing the paired signature); and the store seam reads both arms from ONE table keyed by world. Fewer than two paired worlds is refused (one difference has no spread — n − 1 is a division by zero), and a pool on which every world moved by the same amount is refused for the same reason arrived at a larger n (a standard error of exactly zero), rather than answered with an infinity that reads like overwhelming evidence. (2) The verdict — rejects_proportion_comparison(proportion, *, arm_size, rate_delta, delta, spread, power=0.80), the shape this member's ladder already uses for a judgment over figures the caller holds (rejects_thin_pool, rejects_uncapped_sweep); it never opens a database, because a verdict is not a count and the count is the caller's. It compares two CAPACITIES: what a two-proportion test of that size, clustered as §11.0 says replays are, would need, against what the paired statistic needs (power_capacity). An arm_size below the PAIRED requirement is refused outright (that is the M3 precondition, and no statistic funds it, so the repair is the pool's: accumulate worlds — and the refusal is what depends_on 278's split feeds). An arm_size BETWEEN the two requirements is refused too, and THAT is the feature's own sentence: the size buys the paired comparison and does not buy the proportion one, so the comparison that works is available and the one being asked for is not. An arm_size that funds the proportion test is ADMITTED — the module forbids a comparison the evidence does not support, and refusing there would be editorialising rather than judging; a refusal that always fired would be wrong. Two effect sizes are SEPARATE required keywords, rate_delta and delta, because §11.0's two worked examples use different quantities on different scales (0.30 → 0.21 is a 0.09 shift between two RATES; ΔIR = 0.3 is a difference between two CONTINUOUS readings), and both formulas take "a difference" — so one keyword serving both would inflate one requirement by (0.3/0.09)² ≈ 11× or shrink the other past the precondition's meaning, returning a plausible integer either way with nothing announcing the substitution. The precondition is asked FIRST and asked of the paired requirement, because that is the figure §12's M3 gate is written against; otherwise an enormous rate_delta could shrink the proportion requirement below its arm size and slip a caller past an unfunded pool. (3) The arithmetic, reproduced rather than quoted — Appendix B's n ≈ 8(σ_diff/Δ)² is power_capacity(delta, *, spread, power), where the 8 is NOT a hard-coded constant but (z_{α/2} + z_β)² at 95%/80%, generalised so a caller states its own power; it rounds UP, because the figure is a requirement and a pool one world short of it does not fund the test. It answers 56 at (0.3, 0.8) — the PRD's "~56 worlds" — and the proportion side is the standard two-sample sizing over §11.0's own rate pair, answering 365 at (0.30, 0.09) against the PRD's "~364 independent commits per arm", ×4 (the named PROPORTION_DESIGN_EFFECT, applied as a multiple rather than modelled because §11.0 gives "well over a thousand" as an order-of-magnitude floor) = 1460, the "well over a thousand". A delta of zero, in either formula, is REFUSED rather than answered with an infinity — for the proportion side it is refused by name rather than left to a division by delta², which would raise the interpreter's own ZeroDivisionError about floats for a fact about the pair of rates — and a rate shift is refused when it would carry a rate off the unit interval. A spread of zero answers zero worlds, deliberately: two arms that read identically everywhere need no worlds to be told apart, and the arithmetic's own value is right. (4) The store seam — paired_pool_difference(candidate_policy, baseline_policy, *, database_url, spread, delta, power, env): name the two arms by their policy_version, resolve the database the deployment names (an explicit URL first, then DATABASE_URL, refused by name when neither does), read each arm's per-world readings from replay_score, and compare them paired. §10.3.1's "same policy pair on the same worlds" is exactly what reading both arms from ONE pool buys: the worlds pair by construction rather than by the caller's bookkeeping. A policy with several rows for one world (several beta readings) takes the last by id, deterministically — never SELECT DISTINCT, which would return two readings for a world and drop one silently at the dict boundary. Refuses a database holding no replay_score table (no pool to compare over) and a policy compared against ITSELF (every difference would be exactly zero — a fact about the comparison, not about the pool, and the arithmetic's own message would describe the pool instead). The comparison WRITES NOTHING: it is a read, so a comparison taken under feature 270's hold is permitted — which is load-bearing for the loop, since §C5 holds the pool fixed for the whole outer iteration and the comparison is what the iteration is for. Two new error SIBLINGS under DreamingError, split by the REPAIR the caller must make: ProportionComparisonError (code proportion_comparison) for the QUESTION being the wrong one (repair: ask for the paired statistic) and PairedComparisonError (code unpaired_worlds) for the question being right and the EVIDENCE not pairing (repair: compare the arms over the worlds that carry both). Neither is feature 275's pool_too_thin, whose repair is grow the pool — a caller catching them together would go looking for more worlds when its statistic was the problem, or be told to switch statistics while holding 40 worlds, which funds neither test. Feature 270's FreezeRequestError from the URL seam is TRANSLATED rather than propagated, so a caller comparing two arms never meets "your hold was malformed" for an act that held nothing. The member's one spellings of the shared rules (sqlite_path, the freezes's URL translation) are reused and translated at this module's seam. No central registry, router, app factory, middleware, settings, or migration is edited, and no table is created or written; no new @register component is added (feature 270's single "dreaming" component is untouched); the member joins by workspace-scan convention and does not import another workspace member. The module is stdlib-only: statistics, math, sqlite3, os.

existing_context.stack: Python 3.12 / uv-workspace (packages/* members, import names are underscored slugs) / pytest (ruff + mypy conventions). The module loader (src/app/module_loader.py) discovers members from the root pyproject.toml `[tool.uv.workspace] members = ["packages/*"]`, imports each package so its module-level `@register` fires, and composes what each `@register` builder contributes under a component name. `app` (src/app) is a namespace package with no `__init__.py`; the seats in src/app/modules/ <member>/ are reached by namespace import (e.g. app.modules.dreaming). A member never imports another member — it reaches shared shapes through `app.*`, never through a sibling package's import name.
existing_context.test_baseline: The repository-level suite under tests/ is collected by pytest with testpaths=tests; each workspace member's own suite lives under packages/<member>/tests/ and is collected under its own conftest (same-basename files collide under one pytest run), and is NOT graded by the bare `uv run pytest` acceptance gate — a member suite must be run explicitly (run both `uv run pytest tests/` and the member's own `packages/dreaming/tests/`). Baseline before this feature: 270 passed in packages/dreaming/tests, 1084 passed at the repository level. The repo lint is red on main (mypy absent, pre-existing ruff errors), so lint only the changed files and compare to a sibling. The dreaming member is stdlib-only, and feature 281 keeps it that way: statistics, math, os, sqlite3.
existing_context.conventions: snake_case modules, hand-written __slots__ value classes for records (this member's FreezeRecord/PoolSplit/CapRecord precedent), docstrings that cite the governing documents by section and quote the sentence they implement, refusals that open with a greppable code prefix and name the repair, error classes split by the repair rather than by where the failure was noticed, and every figure the PRD states reproduced from its formula rather than quoted. The member's honesty stance: a module cites the document it implements and says what it is NOT (this one is not a component, holds nothing, writes nothing, and speaks for neither the pool's size nor the ladder).
existing_context.context: existing modules in packages/dreaming/src/dreaming/: errors.py (the member's vocabulary), layout.py (the pool's restated shape), cycle.py (feature 270's freeze, and sqlite_path), ladder.py (feature 275, the floor), ceiling.py (feature 276), cap.py (feature 277), split.py (feature 278, the 70/30 train/holdout split this feature's precondition consumes). Tests live in packages/dreaming/tests/ with their own conftest.py providing database_url, pool, scores and freeze fixtures.

deliverables.deliverable: packages/dreaming/src/dreaming/paired.py — the statistic, the verdict and the store seam, with PAIRED_CODE, PAIRED_LEVEL, POWER, PROPORTION_CODE and PROPORTION_DESIGN_EFFECT as module constants; paired_ir_difference, paired_pool_difference, rejects_proportion_comparison, power_capacity and PairedDifference in __all__. No @register, no table, no write.

packages/dreaming/tests/test_paired.py — the feature's own suite, with the arithmetic pinned against §11.0's derived figures rather than against the module re-run, the pairing refusals, the band's three outcomes, the two-effect-size separation and the store seam; test_errors.py extended with the sibling pin against the member's whole vocabulary; test_cross_member.py extended with the read pinned against 0109's own executed DDL.
